1: a brief html page for Entrepreneur First. I want to display What i can do across 7 days as a part of the challenge. 
What is the EF-Start challenge?

EF-Start is an exceptionally challenging 7-day remote experience designed to accelerate your entrepreneurial career. You will design an ambitious agenda for your week, and then spend 7 days delivering on it. You will be in a cohort of other exceptional future founders who will support and challenge you through your week.

What will I do during the challenge? 

Through the week, you will work on your agenda individually. We have the following group touch-points: 
Kick-off call;
Daily stand-ups;
Upload a short video each day to track your progress;
Provide further evidence of your progress each day;
Upload final presentations. 

In addition, we are interested in how you are able to support and challenge others, and identify exceptional talent. You should allocate roughly 3h over the week to giving feedback to your peers on our platform. You will also be invited to a Discord community for realtime collaboration. 

What should I work on?

We encourage Starters to define their own challenge. It is important that: 
Your challenge is ambitious, yet can feasibly be done in a heroic lift over 7 days. 
It should demonstrate (or help you refine) your edge.
It is on your path. If you do this challenge and we don’t select you, you will have no regrets because the work will make you more likely to succeed anyhow.

content.text: What else have i missed? Interview me if needed?

You have the thesis and outcome. What’s missing is the evidence plan: what will make “commit” vs. “move on” a real decision, not a feeling?

For EF, I’d want to pin down:

1. Who will test it during the seven days—real Obsidian users, founders, friends—and how many?
2. What is the smallest working demo? For example: an Obsidian plugin that notices a blocker and offers one reflection question.
3. What specific signal earns commitment: 3 people install it? 2 use it again unprompted? A willingness to pay? A strong qualitative reaction?
4. What is your personal edge here—technical ability, a particular insight from your own workflow, access to users, or taste in interaction design?
5. What will you show daily as evidence: product clips, user interviews, test results, or shipped iterations?
6. How will you reconcile open source/adoption with collecting behavioral data? This is central to a privacy-first product, even if the seven-day answer is simply “opt-in, local-first telemetry later.”
7. What is the initial wedge: Obsidian specifically, or “ambient AI for deep work” more broadly?

The page should probably include a short “How I’ll know” section once you answer #3. That makes the challenge read as a founder experiment rather than a beautiful product concept.

2: an Obsidian plugin for now for maximum exposure; might need a new UI or borrow from a diff. Key product: invisible suggestion. 3: perhaps Obisidan marketplace? If not, then the github stars... 7 days ambitious goal: get my first 10 users (coming from someone who doesnt do GTM... thsi would be interesting). 4: technical ability + taste, but ignore that... What we want is a simple page that showcase 1) what we aim to do in 7 days and 2) what is the product. 5: ignore for now. 6: ignore for now. 7: ignore from now

That narrows it well: this is a concise founder challenge statement, centered on one measurable outcome—ship an Obsidian plugin and reach the first 10 users—alongside the “invisible suggestion” product idea. I’ll simplify the page around those two points and render-check it.
